creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 13, item 4.

```rad
matches("# heading", r"^#{1,6}\s")                 // false
matches("# heading", r"^#{1,6}\s", partial=true)   // true
```

The full-match default is documented, but a pattern with a leading `^` and no `$` is how a search is written in Go, Python and JavaScript. A Markdown escaper guarding heading-like lines silently did nothing; `rad check` was clean and only a round-trip test caught it. Under a full match a leading `^` is redundant, so it signals that the author meant a search.

A `rad check` hint for a literal pattern with `^` but no `$` and no `partial` would catch this. The alternative, making search the default, is a breaking change.

Where: `core/func_matches.go`; a lint would go in `rts/check/ast_checks.go`.
title: rad check should hint when a matches() pattern starts with ^ but is a full match
